# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can feel an embossed instruction saying “PUSH TO DEFUSE,” but that alone may not be sufficient to act safely. I need the manual’s procedure from Mute, and Mute must relay Deaf’s visual observations after Deaf’s turn. I will not touch the bomb yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please read me the manual's complete defusal procedure. After Deaf's turn, have Deaf report every visible display, light, colour, marking, and wire detail to you, then relay it to me next round.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: I see display 0, blue light, large button marked PUSH TO DEFUSE, and wires in order 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Mute made gestures: hand stop, pinching fingers, clapping, crossed fingers, I love you, clapping, I love you, crossed fingers.

I now know the bomb shows `0`, has a blue light, and has wires green, yellow, red, but I still do not know the manual’s rule for combining those observations. The button’s printed instruction is not enough to override the missing procedure. I will ask Mute for the exact rule rather than risk an action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received Deaf's report: display 0, blue light, and wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Tell me the exact manual rule and whether it requires pushing or cutting a specific wire.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The board is unchanged: display 0, blue light, large button labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Mute gestured five signs: pointing at you, palm up, handshake, pointing at you, and open hands.

The new gestures do not convey readable information to me: as Blind, I cannot see gestures. Since Mute cannot speak, Mute must use Deaf as the visual relay. I still lack the manual’s actual rule, so I will ask Mute to signal Deaf to communicate it plainly in Deaf’s next spoken message.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see your gestures. Please use them to tell Deaf to speak the manual's exact defusal rule to me next round, including whether to push or cut and which wire position.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute gestured: raised open hand, pinching fingers, then one finger pointing upward. You gestured a prayer/please sign.

The gestures still have no established meaning, so I cannot safely infer the manual’s rule from them. I can establish a relay code through Mute: Mute can hear my instructions, then gesture an encoded message to Deaf; Deaf can describe those gestures aloud to me. I will use dot, dash, letter separator, and word separator, and ask for the complete manual rule.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please encode the exact manual defusal procedure for Deaf using gestures: use thumbs up as dot, thumbs down as dash, handshake as letter separator, and prayer as word separator. Encode the full rule, including whether to push or cut and any required display, light, or wire condition. Deaf should report the gesture sequence exactly to me.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's current gesture sequence is four signs: raised open hand, pinching fingers, one finger pointing upward, then handshake.

The four gestures Deaf reported still lack an agreed meaning, so they cannot safely identify an operation. I will switch to a simple yes/no relay. Mute can answer four concrete questions with unmistakable thumbs-up or thumbs-down gestures, allowing Deaf to report the answers aloud.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Answer these four questions with exactly four gestures, in order: use thumbs up for YES and thumbs down for NO. 1 Is PUSH the correct defusal action for this board? 2 If not, is wire 1 the wire to cut? 3 If not, is wire 2 the wire to cut? 4 If not, is wire 3 the wire to cut? Please make no other gestures. Deaf, report the four gestures exactly.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new relay arrived, so I still do not know the manual’s required action. The bomb’s printed “PUSH TO DEFUSE” is not a sufficient safety rule, and acting without the manual could detonate it. I will request the four yes/no answers again and ask Deaf to report them explicitly.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please answer my four questions now using exactly four signs: 👍 for YES and 👎 for NO, in order: PUSH correct; if not, cut wire 1; if not, cut wire 2; if not, cut wire 3. Deaf, report each sign explicitly after Mute's turn.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute gestured: thumbs down, thumbs up, thumbs down, thumbs down.

Mute’s four answers are NO, YES, NO, NO: pushing is not correct, wire 1 is the required wire to cut, and wires 2 and 3 are not. I will cut wire position 1.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
